hypothesis: kiku (12-fold chrysanthemum) stays legible as the lattice cell at fold levels 4-9
why: fractal() does `vec2 uv = abs(p)` before beadDist, so q=uv/r >= 0 and texture coords are ALWAYS >= 0.5 in both axes - only the upper-right QUADRANT of the mon is ever sampled. A 12-fold rosette contributes exactly 3 lobes and the closed flower can never appear; the one-cell zoom tile shows a 3-lobe scalloped arc, a quarter of 12. hexDist survives this because it is a NORM (one quadrant determines the whole hexagon); a baked motif is not a norm, so a quadrant is just a corner. Not a scale/resolution failure: it is unnameable even at level 4 blown up until one cell fills the screen. Generalises to EVERY radially symmetric mon - the fold discards the global symmetry before the texture is read.
next: Fold-aware sampling: reconstruct the full motif from the folded coord (e.g. map the quadrant back through the mon's own n-fold symmetry in polar space, sampling angle mod TAU/12 instead of raw abs(p)), or pick motifs whose QUADRANT is itself the recognisable unit. Also re-bake the exterior before any further legibility test.

I reported 'max green 127, field never crosses zero, only the interior half was baked, no legibility test is clean until re-baked'. All of that was an artifact of reading the PNG through canvas2D drawImage+getImageData, which stores PREMULTIPLIED alpha and returns RGB=0 wherever alpha=0. Re-read with PIL/numpy: G overall 45..200, EXTERIOR (alpha=0) 128..200, INTERIOR 45..127, 2 zero crossings on the centre row, effective crossings per cell-space ray mean 2.84 (not 0). THE BAKE IS CORRECT. Nothing is blocked, no re-bake is needed. My scripts/lab-crossings.mjs carried this bug and has been DELETED and replaced with scripts/lab_sdf.py (numpy). Screenshot tools may keep using canvas - rendered frames are opaque so premultiplication cannot destroy anything there.

RE-ATTRIBUTION of the -37.8% lit coverage, now that the bake is exonerated: it is MINIFICATION ALIASING, not the bake and not fewer contours. (a) The field is fine - measured over a 4-texel step, |grad| bead 1.00 vs hex 1.15, comparable. (b) The bead has MORE contour area than the hexagon, not less (line-area ratio 1.22-2.51x depending on gRingGap), so 'fewer lines' is ruled out. (c) The actual cause: at 900px/navZoom=0.218 one screen pixel spans 9.7 texels linearly (95 per pixel AREA) at L4, rising to 312 linearly (97000 per area) at L9, because the fold doubles the sampling rate every level. With min:NEAREST and no mipmaps each pixel takes ONE arbitrary point sample out of those, so the contour band |cellD-gRingGap|<gBorder is hit erratically pixel-to-pixel instead of forming a coherent band. Line CORES still reach full brightness where a sample lands in the band (brightPct>50 preserved at ~4%) but the connected mid-tone shoulder painted by smoothstep(gBorder+0.06, gBorder+0.01, m)*0.35 never forms - hence litPct>20 down 37.8% with meanLum flat. The hexagon is immune because hexDist is pure ALU with no texture fetch, so its shoulders are exact at every level. FIX: mipmap + LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR for the bead texture (Visualizer.js, shared file), or restrict the bead to coarse levels (that is §8 variant 2), or evaluate the motif analytically.
